title: Conditionals and consequences
function: Talk about conditions and hypothetical results

sections.heading: What is a conditional?
sections.body: A conditional sentence has two parts: the condition (if clause) and the result (main clause). There are different types depending on how real or imaginary the situation is.

sections.heading: Zero conditional (general truths)
sections.body: If + present simple, present simple. Used for facts that are always true.
list: If you heat water, it boils.
If I don't sleep, I feel tired.
If you press this button, the machine stops.

sections.heading: First conditional (real future)
sections.body: If + present simple, will + base verb. Used for possible future situations.
list: If it rains, I will stay at home.
If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
If we leave now, we will arrive on time.

sections.heading: Second conditional (imaginary present)
sections.body: If + past simple, would + base verb. Used for hypothetical or imaginary situations.
list: If I had more money, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologise.
If she spoke English, she would get the job.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'will' after 'if': 'If it will rain' is wrong. Say 'If it rains'.
Do not use 'would' in the if clause in second conditional: 'If I would have' is wrong. Say 'If I had'.
In second conditional with 'I', use 'were' not 'was' (formal).

list.definition: If we don't reduce pollution, the planet will suffer.
If we recycle more, we will help the environment.
If we don't act, climate change will get worse.
If we save energy, we will reduce costs.
If we use less plastic, the oceans will be cleaner.
If we protect forests, we will save many species.
If I make the right choice, things will improve.
If you work hard, the result will be good.
If we plan now, the future will be better.
If you take this opportunity, your life will change.
If I make a mistake, I will learn from it.
If I were you, I would take the job.
If I had a car, I would drive everywhere.
If I could fly, I would visit every country.
What would you do if you won the lottery?

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: If you heat water, it boils.
If it rains, I will stay at home.
If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
If I had more money, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologise.
If she spoke English, she would get the job.
If we leave now, we will arrive on time.
What would you do if you won the lottery?
questions: In sentence 1, what type of conditional is it and why?
In sentences 2, 3 and 7, which tense is used in the if clause and which in the main clause?
In sentences 4, 5 and 6, what is the difference from first conditional?
In sentence 5, why is 'were' used instead of 'was'?
In sentence 8, why is 'would' used in the question?

questions.prompt: If I ___ you, I would apologise.
questions.explanation: In second conditional with I/he/she we use were.

questions.prompt: If you study hard, you ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

questions.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: Do not use 'will' after 'if'. Use present simple.

questions.prompt: If I ___ more time, I would learn Italian.
If you heat ice, it ___ .
If she ___ English, she would get the job.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: past simple in if clause.

questions.prompt: We ___ arrive on time if we leave now.
questions.explanation: First conditional: will in main clause.

questions.prompt: If I ___ the lottery, I would buy a house.
If you don't water plants, they ___ .
questions.explanation: Zero conditional: general truth. Both 'die' and 'will die' possible but 'die' is more natural for a general fact.

questions.prompt: What ___ you do if you saw a ghost?

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 first conditional sentences about your plans for next year. Use 'If + present, will + verb'.
Write 5 second conditional sentences about imaginary situations. Use 'If I had/were... I would...'.
Write 3 pieces of advice for a friend using 'If I were you, I would...'.

questions.prompt: If it ___ , we will cancel the picnic.
questions.explanation: First conditional: present simple after if.

questions.prompt: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ___ .
She ___ pass if she studies more.
questions.explanation: First conditional: will in main clause.

questions.prompt: If I ___ you, I would take the job.
If we ___ now, we will catch the train.
What would you do if you ___ a lot of money?
If I had a car, I ___ drive to work.
If you don't eat, you ___ hungry.
If she ___ harder, she would pass.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Zero: If + present, present. General truths.
First: If + present, will + verb. Real future.
Second: If + past simple, would + verb. Hypothetical.
Do NOT use 'will' after 'if'.
In second conditional, use 'were' with I/he/she (formal).

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'If it will rain'. Say 'If it rains'.
Do not say 'If I would have'. Say 'If I had'.
Do not confuse first and second conditionals.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: If you..., I will...
If I were you, I would...
What would you do if...?
If I had..., I would...
